changes_made.explanation: Changed answer from Yes to No because this paper focuses on pronoun coreference resolution (NLU task), not natural language generation. Removed 'Dialogue Generation' from tasks as it's only mentioned as a downstream application, not evaluated.

Changed answer from No to Yes because the paper explicitly uses automatic metrics (Precision, Recall, F1 for in-text PCR; R@1, R@5, R@10 for out-of-text PCR) to evaluate coreference resolution performance.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. The models mentioned (BERT, SpanBERT, ELMo-LSTM) are used for coreference resolution, not for evaluation.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The paper relies solely on automatic metrics for evaluation.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on pronoun coreference resolution (NLU task) rather than natural language generation. While it mentions dialogue generation as a downstream application, it does not actually generate or evaluate dialogue outputs. The paper uses standard coreference evaluation metrics but no human or LLM-based evaluation.
